grants.title: Permissions
grants.description: Permissions given to a member by name, or to a position — a department at some of its levels — on top of what the staff positions already give.
grants.formHint: Fill in a VID for one member, a department and its levels for whoever holds that position, or tick the team of a FIR and choose its levels: only one of the three. A permission scoped to no department is held on every one of them. Given to a member, a permission on a department also lets them see what that department keeps to itself; given to a position on another department, or to the team of a FIR, it gives the permission there and nothing else of the department. A deny always wins over a grant.

delete.description: Only an award nobody has received can be deleted. One somebody holds is retired instead: untick «Active».

awardSignals.title: Award queue
awardSignals.description: Members the hub points out for an award. A person decides, always.

awardAssignments.title: Assigned awards
awardAssignments.description: Who received which award, why, and who decided.
awardAssignments.formHint: Assign the award on IVAO as well: the member sees it on their IVAO profile, and this register keeps who decided and why.

delete.title: Revoke this assignment?
delete.description: It leaves the register; the audit log keeps what it was. Remember to take it back on IVAO too.

map.label: Map of the legs
map.noWebgl: This browser cannot draw the map (WebGL2 is off or unavailable). The legs are listed below.

discord.title: Discord
discord.privacy: The hub keeps your Discord username and id, and asks Discord for nothing else. You see them here and no other member does; the division may use the id to recognise you on its Discord server. You can disconnect whenever you want.

refused.taken: That Discord account is connected to another member. Disconnect it there first.
refused.failed: The connection with Discord did not complete. Please try again.

tokens.title: My tokens
tokens.description: A program of yours — the validator's agent — signs in with a token instead of your browser. It opens what the program needs and nothing else, and it works with your permissions as they are today.
tokens.noAudience: None of your programs can use a token: they come with the permissions that need one.

hints.name: Where it will live, so you recognise it later: "home PC".
hints.days: From 1 to 90. When it expires, make a new one.

issued.title: The token "{{name}}" is ready
issued.description: Copy it into your program now: the hub will not show it again. If you lose it, revoke it and make another.
issued.label: The token

revoke.title: Revoke this token?
revoke.description: The program using "{{name}}" stops working on its next request. This cannot be undone.
